- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–30% for high sentiment periods.
- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast by 10–25% for low sentiment periods.
- Model often overshoots after sharp sentiment spikes (e.g., sentiment jumps to 1.00+); apply a “cool-down” factor: cap forecast at 1.5x recent high or 2x prior day’s value if sentiment >0.8.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: if 3+ consecutive days show high forecast error, adjust next forecast toward historical mean of last 7 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; apply a 10–15 day smoothing filter to sentiment before weighting forecast.
- If sentiment history shows alternating high/low cycles, model tends to misalign with sentiment direction; align forecast slope with sentiment trend direction (e.g., if sentiment rising, forecast should rise; if falling, forecast should fall).
- When true outcome shows rapid decline after spike, model often fails to recognize “sell-off” sentiment; reduce forecast by 20–40% if sentiment drops sharply after a peak.
